perspective-emotion/perspective-taking.reason: Several independent read experiments; no failed large replication found (searched). A p-curve analysis calls the stereotype results 'mixed' but found 'some evidential value' despite 'low statistical power', which fits B and rules out A.

sources.cite: Huang, Peng & Simmons (2021), Group Processes & Intergroup Relations

perspective-emotion/perspective-getting.reason: The 'Asking them does' half rests on one final experiment, with no independent replication.

perspective-emotion/self-distancing.reason: The pre-registered meta-analysis (g = 0.19) flags risk-of-bias uncertainty; no failed large replication found (searched). Tie-break 7 keeps the grade with effect small.

perspective-emotion/expressive-writing.reason: Tie-break 3: the meta-analyses materially disagree. Mogk et al. 2006 (30 RCTs): 'Neither regarding somatic nor psychological health variables significant effect sizes were found'. Reinhold, Bürkner & Holling 2018 (39 RCTs): 'Expressive writing did not yield significant long-term effects on depressive symptoms'. Both stand against Frattaroli's r = .075. The most recent read synthesis, Guo 2023 (31 RCTs), finds a 'small but significant effect (Hedges' g = -0.12)', which leaves the conflict open, so at most B. No bias-corrected estimate near zero was found, so not C. Effect stays small. The claim is supporting, so no displayed grade changes.

sources.cite: Mogk, Otte, Reinhold-Hurley & Kröner-Herwig (2006), GMS Psycho-Social-Medicine (no DOI; Europe PMC PMC2736499)
Reinhold, Bürkner & Holling (2018), Clinical Psychology: Science and Practice
Guo (2023), British Journal of Clinical Psychology

perspective-emotion/ritual-cadence.reason: No read source tests any monitoring cadence, and Burke et al. 2011 says the required dose is unknown.

perspective-emotion/ritual-duration.reason: One small read experiment (Burton & King 2008). Reinhold et al. 2018 reports larger effects 'when the number of sessions was higher'; that concerns session count, not session length, and does not change the grade.

perspective-emotion/decatastrophizing.reason: The forecasting half is supported; the intervention half has only one indirect test, from overlapping authors.

perspective-emotion/gratitude.reason: The only read source is Emmons & McCullough 2003; nothing read addresses the weekly-versus-daily half.

perspective-emotion/intrapersonal-goal-c.reason: The resolution half, which is what the two-sides page does, is untested; the nearest read evidence (Miller & Rose) warns against a neutral two-sided exercise.

perspective-emotion/domain-satisfaction.reason: Reliability rests on one peer-reviewed multi-study paper plus an instrument manual (practice); the 'shows which domain drives a change' half is untested.
